title: PPL .fit() on a distribution whose parameters are all constants is a silent no-op (result=None, no warning); three shipped notebooks now print unfitted likelihoods, one of them a false claim
surface: mixle.ppl Poisson/NegativeBinomial/StudentT .fit(); notebooks/applications/bayesian_tweet_rhythm.ipynb cell 9, option_pricing_and_implied_volatility.ipynb cell 23, fake_news_detection.ipynb cell 13
reproduction: cd <review-root>/reviews-081/pass-07 && <review-root>/candidate-081/venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Poisson, NegativeBinomial, free; x=list(np.random.RandomState(0).poisson(14.8,164).astype(float)); m=Poisson(2.0).fit(x); print(m.dist.lam, m.result); print(Poisson(free).fit(x).dist.lam); print(NegativeBinomial(2.0,0.5).fit(x).dist)" ; then …/python atk_tweet_ll.py
expected: Either the constants are treated as initial values and fitted (the behaviour the stored June outputs show: tweet cell 9 'Poisson -934 vs negative binomial -594' equals the scipy MLE log-likelihoods -933.67 / -593.81 on the same 164 counts) or .fit() refuses/warns that there is nothing to fit.
observed: Poisson(2.0).fit(x) -> lam stays 2.0, .result is None, no warning; NegativeBinomial(2.0,0.5).fit -> unchanged. Fresh tweet output: 'total log-likelihood: Poisson -3706 vs negative binomial -1502; AIC favours NB by -4406' (both models unfitted at lam=2, r=2,p=0.5; scipy at lam=2 gives -3706.08 exactly). observed: build returns GeneratedNumbaKernel, encode works, zero warnings. engine_benchmarks prints 'N= 2000 numpy 0.0007 numba 0.0050 torch 0.0022 ... N=200000 numpy 0.0249 numba 0.3833 torch 0.0244' (the 'numba fused' line is 7-15x slower than numpy) and import_and_warmup prints 'cold numba cache (recompile all): 1.78 s / warm 2.84 s / on-disk cache saves ~0.6x' as if a cache were in play. ppl_scaling's headline '76x' becomes '4x'.
